content.title: 200/1200 Public Promotional Housing (LPP)
summary: Delivery of 200 residential units within the wider 1,200-home Sidi Abdallah master programme, integrating public promotional housing (LPP) with ground-floor commercial and professional premises.

The development introduces high-density residential blocks configured as ground floor plus 9 upper floors (R+9), accommodating F3 and F4 apartment layouts alongside active street-level commercial frontage.
description: The construction scope focused on the execution of secondary trades and interior fit-out works for the dense residential blocks. Facade articulation, internal circulation cores, and technical services were coordinated to align with the master plan's structural and spatial constraints.

By integrating ground-floor retail and professional spaces directly beneath the R+9 residential massing, the architectural layout establishes a functional mixed-use profile that supports local economic activity within the urban pole.
content.authority: A public housing delivery where secondary trades, service premises, and R+9 density work together to support a new urban district.

facilityGroups.title: Project Programme
items: 200 LPP residential units delivered within a 1,200-home master plan
R+9 residential blocks containing F3 and F4 apartment layouts
Completed in 2022 in compliance with national technical standards

faq.question: What is the scope of the 200/1200 LPP housing project?
faq.answer: It comprises the delivery of 200 public promotional housing (LPP) units, configured with ground-floor commercial spaces, within a larger 1,200-unit urban development in Sidi Abdallah.

faq.question: What construction works were executed on this site?
faq.answer: The contract encompassed secondary trades and interior fit-out works for the R+9 residential blocks, excluding the primary roads and utility networks (VRD) package.

faq.question: How are the residential buildings configured?
faq.answer: The buildings are structured as ground floor plus 9 upper floors (R+9), containing F3 and F4 apartment layouts designed to integrate with the surrounding urban pole.
